players.product: Semiconductor-related adhesive tapes and semiconductor-related devices

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (April 2025 - March 2026): net sales JPY 319,385 million (up 1.1%) as semiconductor and electronic component-related products continued to perform firmly on increased AI-related demand; operating income JPY 25,156 million (up 2.4%) on higher sales volumes despite higher raw material and fuel prices and higher fixed costs including personnel costs; ordinary income JPY 25,666 million (down 1.6%); net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 17,374 million (up 20.0%). Management states net sales, operating income and net income attributable to owners of the parent were record highs, mainly as semiconductor and electronic component-related products continued to perform well.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales JPY 319,385 million (+1.1%); operating income JPY 25,156 million (+2.4%); net income JPY 17,374 million (+20.0%)

quarterly_data.signal: Electronic and Optical Products segment, FY2026: net sales JPY 100,726 million (up 4.6%) despite the closure of the Korean and Taiwanese subsidiaries, as semiconductor and electronic component-related products performed well; operating income JPY 22,120 million (up 19.5%) on higher sales volumes of those products, although fixed costs such as depreciation of new equipment installed to strengthen the production-increase system rose. Advanced Materials Operations net sales JPY 92,809 million (up 9.2%): semiconductor-related devices decreased slightly, while semiconductor-related adhesive tapes performed well on increased AI-related demand. Optical Materials Operations net sales JPY 7,916 million (down 30.0%): adhesive tapes for OLED displays were flat year on year, but sales fell with the closure of the Korean and Taiwanese subsidiaries.
quarterly_data.figure: segment net sales JPY 100,726 million (+4.6%); operating income JPY 22,120 million (+19.5%); Advanced Materials Operations JPY 92,809 million (+9.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: Other segments, FY2026: Printing and Industrial Materials Products net sales JPY 182,644 million (down 1.1%) and operating income JPY 1,979 million (down 63.8%), hit in Japan by higher raw material, fuel and logistics costs and higher fixed costs and in the US by higher fixed costs and worse process yields; Paper and Converted Products net sales JPY 36,014 million (up 2.8%) and operating income JPY 977 million (up 82.6%), as release papers (mainly for electronic materials) were firm and release films for optical-related products and process papers for carbon-fiber composite materials recovered.
quarterly_data.figure: Printing and Industrial Materials JPY 182,644 million (-1.1%), operating income JPY 1,979 million (-63.8%); Paper and Converted JPY 36,014 million (+2.8%), operating income JPY 977 million

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 production (at manufacturing cost, approximate): total JPY 247,179 million (down 0.8%), of which Electronic and Optical Products JPY 63,884 million (down 2.2%), Printing and Industrial Materials Products JPY 140,577 million (0.0%), Paper and Converted Products JPY 42,717 million (down 1.4%). The company states that most products and merchandise are shipped as soon as orders are received, so orders received are almost the same as sales.
quarterly_data.figure: production JPY 247,179 million (-0.8%); Electronic and Optical Products JPY 63,884 million (-2.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 net sales by customer location: Japan JPY 118,964 million, China JPY 35,206 million, other Asia JPY 59,644 million, United States JPY 86,879 million, other JPY 18,689 million (total JPY 319,385 million). China is now shown separately because it exceeded 10% of net sales. No single customer accounts for 10% or more of net sales, so the report names no major customers.
quarterly_data.figure: Japan JPY 118,964 million; China JPY 35,206 million; Asia JPY 59,644 million; US JPY 86,879 million; other JPY 18,689 million

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced Materials Operations outlook for FY2027 (year ending March 2027): the company forecasts that strong demand will continue for high-performance semiconductors such as HBM and for AI data centers, and expects higher sales of semiconductor-related adhesive tapes and devices and of multilayer ceramic capacitor-related tape; it will work to establish a supply system able to meet the demand increase by stabilizing raw material procurement and strengthening its production system, and aims to make the CNT pellicle for EUV lithography tools, which it is moving into mass production, a new business pillar of the division by building out its sales system.

Management outlook for FY2027: global growth is expected to continue on active AI-related investment and fiscal policies, but concerns about a slowdown are rising from high US tariffs and Middle East tensions; management states the impact of higher raw material, fuel and logistics costs caused by the Middle East situation is extremely large and the possibility of procurement disruptions in the supply chain cannot be ruled out, and that higher fixed costs from wage increases and depreciation of new production equipment will weigh on profit. FY2027 is the final year of the medium-term plan LSV 2030-Stage 2 (April 2024 - March 2027); the long-term vision LSV 2030 targets, for the year ending March 2030, an operating margin of 12% or more and ROE of 10% or more.
quarterly_data.figure: FY ending March 2030 targets: operating margin 12% or more; ROE 10% or more

quarterly_data.signal: R&D, FY2026: total R&D expenses JPY 11,293 million, of which Electronic and Optical Products JPY 6,688 million. For wafer-level packaging driven by generative AI, the company developed the PCBL (Pattern Coating Before Lamination) process, which coats UV-curable resin on the wafer periphery to reduce thickness variation and cracking in back-grinding of bumped wafers, together with the matching resin coating equipment RAD-3400F/12; it continues to develop and propose high-performance dicing tapes, back-grinding tapes and dicing die-bonding tapes for generative-AI devices, HBM-based advanced packages, intelligent sensors using thin wafers and 3D NAND flash memory. Its Nano-Science & Technology Center (Texas, US) focuses on carbon nanotube research and applied products.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 11,293 million; Electronic and Optical Products R&D JPY 6,688 million

quarterly_data.signal: Capex, FY2026: total JPY 15,284 million, mainly: completed the expansion of process-paper coating equipment at the Komatsushima plant (new coating equipment started operating there in September 2025); continued restructuring of the production base at the Ina Technology Center; started construction to build a mass-production system for EUVL pellicles; started construction of a new Advanced Development Center and of new equipment for new-material development; continued environmental equipment work. Planned: Ina Technology Center (Printing and Industrial Materials / Electronic and Optical Products) restructuring, budget JPY 2,450 million, JPY 1,320 million already paid, started November 2024, completion scheduled September 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: capex JPY 15,284 million; Ina Technology Center budget JPY 2,450 million (JPY 1,320 million paid), completion September 2026

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026: multilayer ceramic capacitor-related tape performed well on increased demand for high-end applications for data centers and smartphones. R&D: the company states MLCC demand is expanding with smartphones and automotive uses plus the growth of AI-driven IT infrastructure and edge devices, and the market for release films for MLCC manufacturing is booming; it is improving the quality and functionality of release films for smaller, higher-performance MLCCs and, anticipating growing demand for AI-related electronic components and market growth in EVs and 5G / 6G, is building a production-increase system.
